result.title: How Much Distribution Shift Can a Clustering Withstand? Exact Split and Merge Certificates for Structured Transports
result.summary: In clustering, the distribution of the population being clustered is often uncertain or changes over time, so the true distribution may shift away from the nominal distribution used to form the clustering. Once the clustering is committed and each member is assigned to a cluster, such shifts may change the distribution of each cluster. They can make a cluster too spread out for one representative at a given resolution, motivating a split, or bring distinct clusters close enough to share a representative at that resolution, motivating a merge. We make these split and merge events precise using a local stability criterion built on the phase-transition analysis in deterministic annealing. This notion of stability enables us to quantify how robust a clustering is against such events. Furthermore, motivated by applications in which uncertainty and population change are structured, we study shifts whose displacements are restricted to a prescribed subspace. The smallest structured shifts that reach the respective thresholds define the split and merge radii, for which we obtain exact semidefinite programming (SDP) reformulations. The split SDP has only two scalar decision variables. These convex reformulations enable us to combine the radii into a robustness certificate for the full clustering that gives the size of the smallest structured shift that reaches any monitored split or merge threshold.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究聚类对分布偏移的稳健性：基于确定性退火相变分析给出局部稳定性准则，用其刻画聚类「分裂」与「合并」事件，并在位移限制在给定子空间的情形下导出精确 SDP 形式的分裂/合并半径，进而组合成全聚类的稳健性证书。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分裂/合并阈值与 SDP 证书这一方法线索，可能可供核查 latent 状态聚类或离散化在视觉输入分布偏移下是否仍然成立，但能否用于高维视觉表征结构尚需人工判断。
